scope: A resource gate on simulated downloads
title: A gate holds its bound
description: In every recorded run the most downloads in flight equalled the declared gate bound, from a bound of 1 to a bound of 24.
claim: The gate never admitted more downloads than its bound: in all 7 recorded runs, with bounds from 1 to 24, the most downloads in flight equalled the bound.

headline.label: recorded runs where the most downloads in flight equalled the gate bound
queued jobs per run, each passing a Network gate and awaiting a simulated download

losses: The gate does not choose its bound for you. A bound set too low serialises the work, and a bound set too high lets a crowded service slow down. Finding the bound is what the tuner is for.

method.workload: 24 jobs are queued at once through a ForEach. Each passes a Network gate and awaits a simulated download of 40 ms. The simulated service stretches the wait once more than 6 downloads are in flight. 7 fixed gate bounds from 1 to 24, one recorded run each, after a warm-up run.
engines: EvalApp pipeline with Gate and ForEach
method.verification: Every job records its own timestamps, and the number of downloads in flight is counted inside the gated step, so the bound is checked against what actually ran.

limits: The work is a simulated wait, not a real network. It shows that the gate and its queue hold the bound, not how any real service behaves.
It checks the gate and does not compare EvalApp with another library.

internal.source: A recorded run of the published EvalApp package with ForEach and a Network gate
